subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated exec for unattended cron and heartbeat runs be modeled as a narrow per-job/heartbeat marker, or folded into the broader Gateway-owned scheduling provenance model?
rationale: The remaining work changes who can grant host-exec authority to unattended internal events and how existing wildcard-based setups upgrade, so automation should not choose the permanent trust boundary.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
options.body: Use this issue as the elevated-exec slice of a Gateway-stamped scheduling provenance contract that also covers heartbeat modification provenance and audit.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add explicit per-job and heartbeat elevated authority fields now, but require create/update authorization, execution audit, and migration semantics in the same design.

options.title: Defer And Document Wildcard Risk
options.body: Keep current wildcard behavior for trusted unattended workflows while documenting the risk and waiting for the broader scheduler provenance decision.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the elevated-exec slice of a Gateway-stamped scheduling provenance contract that also covers heartbeat modification provenance and audit.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged authority-boundary work is the caller-agent cron scoping PR, which makes joshavant the best routing candidate for the cron side of the decision.
